courses.title: Microeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Calculus and set theory based presentation of microeconomic theory including consumer and producer theory as well as general equilibrium models.

courses.title: Macroeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of aggregate national economic activities using dynamic models.
courses.prerequisites: EC 4403 or EC 403; and EC 5503 or EC 503.

courses.title: Graduate Econometrics I
courses.description: Specification and statistical inference in econometric models; estimation, verification and prediction of economic variables; recent empirical studies, advanced topics in econometrics.

courses.title: Graduate Econometrics II
courses.description: Specification and statistical inference in econometric models; estimation, verification and prediction of economic variables; recent empirical studies, advanced topics in econometrics.

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of demand and supply. Consumer choice analysis. Income and substitution effects. Firm profit maximization and industry structure. Economic efficiency and welfare effects of policy instruments. Corequisite(s): EC 4401A .

courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Overview of the micro foundations of macroeconomic models and use of these models to understand decisions of consumers, firms, and the government. Includes study of labor market dynamics and wages. Measurement of national accounts and the determinants of economic growth.

courses.title: Mathematical Economics
courses.description: Mathematical description and derivation of micro- and macroeconomic theory.
courses.prerequisites: EC 2201 or EC 201; EC 2202 or EC 220; and MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 1250 or MAT 125; or Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Introduction to econometrics, with a focus on understanding and applying the classical linear regression model; emphasis placed on applications of regression analysis; quantitative model-building; estimation, verification, and prediction of economic variables. Corequisite(s): EC 4444A .

courses.title: International Finance
courses.description: Advanced topics in international liquidity and finance theory. Problems of international monetary systems. Balance of payments theory and practices; theory of exchange rates and mechanism of international adjustment.

courses.title: Capital Markets I
courses.description: Topics in monetary and capital theory. Liquidity creation, financial intermediation and capital formation. Development of capital policy.

courses.title: Capital Markets II
courses.description: Topics in monetary and capital theory. Liquidity creation, financial intermediation and capital formation. Development of capital policy.

courses.title: Graduate Public Finance
courses.description: Public policies, principles, and standards of taxation and expenditures, budgeting, public goods, income redistribution, regulation, and development. Examine the equity and efficiency of public policy and assess the fiscal impact.

courses.title: Graduate Research Practicum I
courses.description: Intensive study of applied research methods and technical writing through replication of existing peer-reviewed findings in the economics literature or through selected research topics determined by the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: EC 5550 or EC 550; and EC 5551 or EC 551; and EC 5503 or EC 503.

courses.title: Graduate Research Practicum II
courses.description: Intensive study of applied research methods and technical writing through replication of existing peer-reviewed findings in the economics literature or through selected research topics determined by the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: EC 5550 or EC 550; and EC 6692 or EC 692.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Independent research and study under the supervision of the faculty. Reporting the research results in the approved form. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 12 units. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and Graduate Writing Assessment passed*.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
